answer: An agent market can make each identity post a refundable bond before it may place bids or receive tasks. The bond is locked on-chain, and a contract slashes it when signed work is not delivered or verified; honest agents recover it after completion. Splitting one agent into many identities then requires funding a separate bond for each, so a sybil attacker must tie up capital and risks losing it per failed identity. An atlas of basalt routes and violet labels would not substitute for that scarce stake.
